name: Cyprus
tagline: The last divided capital in Europe, on an island of Byzantine churches and mountain wine.
summary: Cyprus is the third-largest Mediterranean island and has been divided since 1974, with a UN buffer zone running through the middle of Nicosia. The Republic controls the south; the north is administered separately and recognised only by Türkiye. Beyond the politics, it holds painted Byzantine churches in the Troodos mountains, Roman mosaics at Paphos, and one of the oldest wine traditions in the world.

season.note: Spring is the island's best season — green, flowering and warm enough to swim by May. July and August are extremely hot inland. The Troodos mountains hold snow and a small ski area in February.

getting_around: No railway at all; buses connect the cities and a car is close to essential for the mountains. Crossing to the north on foot at Ledra Street in Nicosia is straightforward for most visitors with a passport, subject to current rules.
food: Meze, twenty or more small plates, ordered for the table and never finished
Halloumi, grilled, which is a protected local product and tastes different here
Commandaria: a sweet wine made the same way since antiquity

festivals.name: Kataklysmos, the flood festival, with water thrown at everyone

know: Crossing points between south and north exist and rules change — check current guidance before planning around one.
The Troodos churches are small, locked and often opened by a neighbour with a key; a donation is expected.

regions.name: Nicosia & the South Coast
regions.summary: The divided capital inland, and the Roman and Hellenistic coast west of Limassol.

cities.name: Nicosia
cities.summary: A Venetian star-shaped fortress city with a UN buffer zone through the middle and a crossing on the main shopping street.
highlights: The Venetian walls, eleven bastions, still tracing the city
The Cyprus Museum's Neolithic and Bronze Age collections
The Ledra Street crossing, and the shuttered street either side of it

experiences.name: The Green Line, walked
experiences.summary: Sandbags, oil drums and 1974 shopfronts, visible from the streets that dead-end into them. Sobering and entirely ordinary to residents.

cities.name: Paphos
cities.summary: A harbour town with Roman villa floors that are among the finest mosaics anywhere, and royal tombs cut into the rock.
highlights: The House of Dionysos and its mosaic floors
Tombs of the Kings, Hellenistic and underground
The Akamas peninsula's empty beaches, north

regions.name: The Troodos Mountains
regions.summary: Painted churches under wooden roofs, vineyards at 1,000 metres, and forest above them.

cities.name: Omodos & the wine villages
cities.summary: Cobbled mountain villages growing indigenous grapes nobody else has, around a 12th-century monastery.
highlights: Xynisteri and mavro, grape varieties grown almost nowhere else
The painted churches of the Troodos, ten of them UNESCO-listed

experiences.name: The barn-roofed painted churches
experiences.summary: Small stone chapels under enormous pitched roofs, frescoed inside floor to ceiling; several need a key fetched from a village house.
